Pupinius , a, um, adj.,
I.Pupinian: “ager,” Cic. Agr. 2, 35, 96 : Pupinia tribus ab agro Pupinio, Paul. ex Fest. p. 232 Müll. (Fest. ib. 233, preserved only in a fragm. form). —Also, Pupiniensis , e, adj.: “ager,” Liv. 9, 41, 10 .—Hence, subst.: Pupinĭa , ae, f. (regio), the Pupinian territory in Latium, a sterile tract of country in the vicinity of Rome, Liv. 26, 9 fin.; Varr. R. R. 1, 9, 5; Col. 1, 4, 2; Val. Max. 4, 4, 4.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
